prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1009; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recording is for claim file purposes. Can you confirm you're comfortable continuing?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Great. Can you walk me through what happened on the day of the accident?

A: I was driving in the left lane on a two-lane road in Houston, heading toward the intersection. The light was green. Then a car came over the center line and hit me head-on. It wasn't going very fast, maybe ten or fifteen miles an hour, but we definitely made contact.

Q: Did your airbags deploy?

A: No, they didn't. The impact felt more like a hard jolt than a crash.

Q: Were you able to get out of the vehicle on your own?

A: Yes, I got out and stood by the car. My neck and upper back felt stiff almost right away.

Q: Did you seek medical attention?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic that same afternoon. They took X-rays and told me I had whiplash. They gave me a neck brace and some anti-inflammatory medication.

Q: How are you feeling now?

A: Still sore. Turning my head to the side hurts, and I get a headache by the end of the day. Sitting at a desk for long periods makes it worse.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?

A: I missed two days and I've been working shorter shifts since then. I'm keeping my doctor's notes.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: Not right now. I just want to get this taken care of and get back to normal.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
